output.summary: The rise in admitted-patient ED length of stay is almost entirely boarding (about 3.0 of 3.2 hours, E5). ED nurse staffing is flat or slightly better (E4), and volume, acuity, admission rate, beds and occupancy are unchanged (E3, E9). Boarding jumped in March and is concentrated in medical-ward boarders, who account for 81% of boarding hours. This coincides with medical-ward discharges moving later, while surgical wards are unchanged (E8, E9). The huddle-day comparison is balanced on workload and shows no spillover to other wards (E11). That supports the discharge-timing hypothesis, though the March change is not directly tested. Travel nurses would not address the mechanism. Pausing the huddle and floating its charge nurse would remove a control that appears to work.
